effect_estimate.comment: Both Poisson proportion ratios (PR) and logistic odds ratios (OR) are reported in Table 1 and Appendices A–B for the quantitative sample (N = 4,218 villages), complemented by qualitative comparative case findings across 7 outlier villages.
effect_estimate.value: In multivariable Poisson regression of 5-year sustained village water system functionality (2014–2018, N = 4,218 villages), log number of community participants at project inception (Community Action Planning) was positively associated with sustainability: crude PR = 1.42 (95% CI: 1.24–1.63, p = 0.000) in Model 1, attenuating to adjusted PR = 1.21 (95% CI: 1.06–1.39, p = 0.005) in Model 2 and PR = 1.21 (95% CI: 1.05–1.38, p = 0.007; corresponding Logit OR = 1.82, 95% CI: 1.42–2.34, p = 0.000) in full Model 3. Collecting tariffs exceeding O&M costs strongly predicted sustainability (Model 3 PR = 1.84, 95% CI: 1.70–2.01, p = 0.000; Logit OR = 6.90, 95% CI: 5.82–8.18, p = 0.000), alongside village revenue per capita (Rp 5,000–Rp 30,000: PR = 1.23, 95% CI: 1.12–1.36, p = 0.000; >Rp 30,000: PR = 1.29, 95% CI: 1.16–1.44, p = 0.000, vs. <Rp 5,000) and non-dug-well water sources (PR = 1.25, 95% CI: 1.08–1.44, p = 0.003). Qualitative deviance analysis across 7 villages showed that collaborative relations between village heads and water user group (KP SPAMS) leaders—providing village resources, facilitating socialization, and granting operational decision space—sustained fee payment and O&M in positive outliers, whereas village head apathy, political rivalry, or elite capture of water points caused non-payment and scheme abandonment in negative outliers.
effect_estimate.where_found: PDF pp. 7–8, Section 2.1 & Table 1; PDF pp. 9–15, Section 2.3; PDF p. 21, Appendix A Table A1; PDF p. 23, Appendix B; PDF p. 28, Appendix C

mechanism_certainty.comment: Under CODEBOOK §9, mixed-methods studies appraised with MMAT have a design ceiling of 2. Rating 2 is warranted because the qualitative fieldwork in 7 positive and negative deviance villages directly documents the frontline administrative and governance mechanisms (village head resource/facility support, socialization facilitation, operational decision space for KP SPAMS vs. elite capture of hydrants and apathy) operating on household fee payment, O&M, and sustained water access, complementing the quantitative association in N = 4,218 villages.

mechanism_flags.comment: Examines community participation in Community Action Planning and post-construction user groups (participation, planning), political/administrative coordination or rivalry/capture between village authorities and KP SPAMS leaders (political_coordination), village authority mobilization of facilities/funds/sub-village leaders to lower socialization and O&M transaction costs (bureaucratic_assistance), operational decision space granted to user group chairs vs. arbitrary capture by village heads (discretion), and household connection fees, O&M tariffs, and informal water charges (fees).
